correctness.rationale: For J_n=K1∨C_n with n rim vertices and n≥6, every edge extends to a two-edge shortest path, so maximal geodesics are exactly spoke–hub–spoke paths for nonadjacent rim pairs and three consecutive rim vertices. With hub absent, uncovered rim vertices must be a clique of the rim cycle, giving z^n+nz^{n−1}+nz^{n−2} for all transversals and exactly nz^{n−2} inclusion-minimal ones. With hub selected, every three consecutive rim vertices must contain a chosen vertex; cyclic unselected gaps g_i∈{0,1,2} yield the all-set enumerator (n/k)[u^{n−k}](1+u+u²)^k. A chosen rim vertex is indispensable precisely for consecutive gap pairs (0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(2,0),(2,1),(2,2); this proves the stated A(u) transfer trace and n/k rooted-set correction, not merely an empirical fit. Every zero-gap forces the following two-gap, giving k≤floor(n/2), while length restrictions give k≥ceil(n/3). For each integer in that range, 1/2-gap words realize it; hub indispensability holds because at least three omitted rim vertices are not a clique. Hence minimal cardinalities are {ceil(n/3)+1,…,floor(n/2)+1}∪{n−2}; for n≥9 the interval gap is ceil(n/2)−4. At the minimum, deficit from 2 per gap yields 3 if n≡0 mod3, n(ceil(n/3)+1)/2 if n≡1 mod3, and n if n≡2 mod3. Independently rebuilt wheel graphs and enumerated all shortest paths and every subset for n=6…11; observed polynomials and multiplicities match. The finite checks alone would not prove all n.

originality.rationale: Primary comparisons credit the original geodesic-transversal definition, the alias maximal-shortest-path cover, the known wheel scalar optimum and the general join-factor dichotomy. The strongest accessible join theorem (Peterin–Semanišin, Theorem 3.5) minimizes among join regimes but does not supply polynomial coefficients, the six local minimality gap pairs or lacunary sizes. Direct Resultary similarity searches found graph cover-free numbers, geodetic polynomials, and dissociation sets for other graph properties rather than this complete census. An unindexed circular 3-path-cover minimal-set enumeration might imply the hub branch, and the 2021 standalone wheel paper was only partially accessible; those are explicit qualified priority risks. These do not, on present evidence, defeat PASS for the combined final exact census and spectrum.

value.rationale: The geodesic-transversal minimum of a wheel was already known. The full all-set and inclusion-minimal generating polynomials, complete cardinality spectrum with a linearly growing missing interval, and explicit congruence-dependent minimum-set multiplicity answer natural structural/counting questions beyond the scalar optimum. The cyclic transfer method enables exact sampling and nonuniqueness analysis for this established graph covering invariant. An all-parameter exact classification is independently useful, not an unmotivated finite graph count.

limitations: Only n≥6 rim vertices and finite undirected simple wheels J_n=K1∨C_n.
Finite independent verification of n=6..11 does not prove all-parameter polynomial identities.
